stem:
Nitin has $14=2\times7$ and $15=3\times5$. He wants to decide whether $14$ and $15$ are co-prime from those prime factorisations.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call them co-prime after looking at the products $14$ and $15$ alone, without checking whether any prime appears in both factorisations.
Also use the same co-prime test to decide whether two fractions are in lowest terms without comparing prime factors, beyond this two-number prime-factor check.
They are co-prime: the primes $2,7$ and $3,5$ share no common prime factor.
Call them co-prime only because $14$ and $15$ are consecutive printed integers, without using the prime factorisations.

teacher.key_rationale: Two numbers are co-prime when their prime factorisations share no prime. Skipping the common-prime check, stretching the test, or grabbing consecutive printed integers all miss that hinge.
